# scripts/sema_must_use_baseline.txt — accepted unchecked-result sites.
#
# Generated by:  python3 scripts/sema_must_use_scan.py --emit-baseline
# Gated by:      scripts/test_adder_must_use.sh
#
# One line per <file>::<caller>::<callee> where `caller` drops the result of
# a `# must_use` `callee`. Line numbers are deliberately absent: they churn
# on every edit above them, and a baseline that churns is a baseline nobody
# re-reads.
#
# SHRINK-ONLY BY INTENT. A site not in this list FAILS the build, and a line
# here that no longer corresponds to a real site also fails (delete it when
# you fix the caller). The list is the debt ledger, not the policy.
#
# TRIAGE. Each entry is classified from reading the caller:
#
#   BUG      the caller does something WRONG when the callee fails: it
#            reports success, advances state, or documents a guarantee it
#            does not check. These are live defects, listed here only
#            because fixing driver/kernel code is outside the scope of the
#            commit that introduced the lint.
#   LATENT   the failure is silent but currently unreachable (the table is
#            statically large enough for the fixed number of callers).
#            Nothing keeps it that way.
#   COVERED  the status is checked, just not at THIS expression — the callee
#            raises a sticky error the caller tests separately.
#   TEST     a selftest's setup step, whose failure the test's own
#            assertions detect on the next line.
#   BOUNDED  provably cannot fail here: a fixed, small number of inserts
#            into a table sized far above it.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# BUG — a partial action reported as a complete one
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# devwsys_keys_write / devwsys_cmd_write push `count` bytes in a loop and then
# `return cast[int64](count)` unconditionally. When the ring fills mid-write
# the tail bytes are DROPPED and write(2) still reports the FULL count. That
# is a short-write POSIX violation and it is the `rm *` shape exactly: a
# partial action reported as complete. The pointer twin at least documents
# "DROP-NEWEST on full" as policy — but its return value still lies.
sys/src/9/port/devwsys.ad::devwsys_keys_write::_wsys_keys_push_byte
sys/src/9/port/devwsys.ad::devwsys_cmd_write::_wsys_cmd_push_wid
sys/src/9/port/devwsys.ad::devwsys_pointer_write::_wsys_ptr_push_byte
# hamslides_key (Ctrl-N / Ctrl-D), _menu_activate and hamslides_hit all
# `return 1` — "handled" — whether or not the slide was actually inserted. At
# MAXSLIDES the keystroke/menu item/click does nothing at all and the UI shows
# no error.
lib/hamslidescore.ad::hamslides_key::hamslides_add_slide
lib/hamslidescore.ad::hamslides_key::hamslides_duplicate_slide
lib/hamslidescore.ad::_menu_activate::hamslides_add_slide
lib/hamslidescore.ad::_menu_activate::hamslides_duplicate_slide
lib/hamslidescore.ad::hamslides_hit::hamslides_add_slide
lib/hamslidescore.ad::hamslides_hit::hamslides_duplicate_slide
# The browser's image decoders: a full image arena means the <img> silently
# renders as nothing, on a page that otherwise looks complete. This is the
# browser-parity failure mode — a wrong render with no diagnostic — arriving
# through a status nobody reads.
user/hambrowse.ad::_decode_images::htmlimg_add
user/hambrowse.ad::_register_demo_image::htmlimg_add
user/hambrowse_gfx_window.ad::_decode_images::htmlimg_add
user/hambrowse_host_gfx.ad::_decode_images::htmlimg_add
user/hambrowse_sdl_host.ad::_decode_images::htmlimg_add
# uffd_read re-queues the message after a failed copy_to_user with the comment
# "Re-queue the message so it is not lost" — and does not check that the
# re-queue succeeded. If the queue is full the message IS lost, and the
# faulting thread waits forever for a fault the monitor never sees. The
# comment states a guarantee the code does not provide.
linux_abi/u_userfaultfd.ad::uffd_read::_uffd_q_push
linux_abi/u_userfaultfd.ad::uffd_pagefault_hook::_uffd_q_push
# virtio_net_init returns success even when the poll list is full, in which
# case this RX queue is NEVER polled — a NIC that is up, configured, and
# receives nothing.
drivers/net/virtio_net.ad::virtio_net_init::napi_register
# _bt_parse_chunk_item `return 1` (parsed OK) even when the chunk map was
# full and the mapping was not recorded; the logical range then reads as
# unmappable much later, far from the cause.
fs/btrfs.ad::_bt_parse_chunk_item::_bt_chunk_add
# SYS_SVC_PUBLISH `return 0` (success) whether or not the name was pushed.
arch/x86/kernel/syscall.ad::do_syscall::name_push
# cgroup_pids_charge_fork: the task stays in its old cgroup and is not
# subject to the limits the caller believes it just applied.
kernel/sched/cgroup_cpu.ad::cgroup_pids_charge_fork::cgroup_cpu_attach
# hamsh `d.get(k, dflt)` stores the default back into the dict and returns it
# as though stored; at LISTELEM_MAX it was not. `d[k] = v` likewise.
user/hamsh.ad::eval_call::v_dict_set
user/hamsh.ad::exec_index_assign::v_dict_set

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LATENT — silent, but not currently reachable
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Three registrations against MAX_CLOCKSOURCES; the table is sized above
# three. A fourth clocksource would be dropped and timekeeping would silently
# keep the worse source.
kernel/time/tick.ad::tick_init::clocksource_register
# hpm reads a channel file line by line into CHANNEL_MAX slots; a long enough
# file silently loses the tail channels.
user/hpm.ad::_channels_load::_channel_add_name
# hamsoftware/hampkgscene feed apt output into a PKG_MAX table. A large
# enough `apt search` result is silently truncated rather than reported as
# truncated.
user/hamsoftware.ad::_scan_registry::hampkg_add_pkg
user/hamsoftware.ad::_feed_line::hampkg_add_search_line
user/hampkgscene.ad::_feed_line::hampkg_add_search_line

# COVERED — the status IS checked, elsewhere

# _argv_push_cstr now rt_raise()s on overflow, and exec_statement /
# run_one_command_x / the `{ }` capture / the for-loop word list all test
# rt_fault() right after _argv_build and refuse to run the command. The
# per-call status is genuinely redundant here — this is what a legitimate
# discard looks like, and it is why the class must stay a lint.
user/hamsh.ad::_argv_push_value::_argv_push_cstr

# The devwsys internal emitters write into a ring they have just sized, and
